svg.title: IV potassium chloride is added for a client in DKA. Which actions does the nurse take? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: Insulin drives potassium into the cells, so potassium is replaced even when the first level is normal. IV potassium is always diluted, on a pump, with cardiac monitoring , and never IV push - a bolus can stop the heart. The kidneys must be making urine so the excess can be excreted.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Diabetes
Read the situation
IV potassium chloride is added for a
client in DKA. Which actions does the
nurse take? Select all that apply.
What fits here
Place the client on a cardiac monitor ·
Give it on an infusion pump · Never give
it by IV push · Infuse no faster than
about 10 mEq/hr through a peripheral line,
per policy · Confirm…
Why it fits
Insulin drives potassium into the cells,
so potassium is replaced even when the
first level is normal. IV potassium is
always diluted, on a pump, with cardiac
monitoring , and never IV push - a bolus
can stop the heart. The kidneys must be
making urine so the excess can be
excreted.
